newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Air mass worth watching for Brazil coffee - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Air mass worth watching for Brazil coffee - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions should warm up slightly in the coming days after a period of cool weather but temperatures could fall sharply next week with the approach of a new air mass, local meteorologists Somar said.
The new air mass is expected to have a center of high pressure of 1,018 millibars over the center of Mato Grosso do Sul and Parana on June 8, said Somar forecaster Marcio Custodio.

While this is not therefore a very strong air mass, it is worth monitoring closely because it is coming in overland and will be arriving when the country's coffee regions are already cool from the effects of last week's air mass, he added.

The center of latest air mass has already left the country some days ago but temperatures have still been cool in the coffee regions, dropping to five degrees Celsius this morning in Pocos de Caldas, traditionally Brazil's coldest coffee region.
In Sao Sebastiao do Paraiso, also in Minas Gerais and another cooler coffee region, the minimum this morning was 8.5 degrees Celsius, the local cooperative said.

The coldest temperatures from the approaching air mass are likely to be seen in the early morning of June 9 as the key regions of Sao Paulo and Minas Gerais are expected to be protected by cloud cover on June 8, Custodio added.
While a more accurate forecast will only be available later this week, current models suggest temperatures could fall to below five degrees Celsius in areas such as Pocos, he said.

"At the moment the models suggest temperatures of around six degrees during the night of June 8 which could mean temperatures of three to four degrees when the dew forms. These are critical levels," Custodio said.
